LESSON_BEGIN
ERROR_CATEGORY: B
TRIGGER_PATTERN: Sector ETF prediction where the model identifies a same-day two-sided macro catalyst (ISM Services) and refuses to pre-score it, futures are flat (ES +0.13% / NQ +0.16%), and the sector has no fresh same-morning catalyst — the model scores all factors zero and predicts flat/flat, but the actual session delivers a broad-market rip (+1.05% SPY) on the macro catalyst beat, producing a large absolute move in the sector ETF that the flat band misses entirely. The model treats "two-sided and unprinted" as a reason to zero out S0/S1 rather than as a reason to widen the magnitude band or reduce confidence in flat, and the tape sleeve (S4) is barred from flipping factors to down but is also not allowed to anticipate an up-side macro surprise.
CURRENT_BEHAVIOR: When a same-day macro catalyst (ISM Services, claims) is identified as two-sided and unprinted, the model encodes it as a confidence/mag cap and zeroes S0/S1, then predicts flat/flat. The tape sleeve is red (1d rel −1.15%) and is treated as confirmation-only, barred from flipping factors to down — but no mechanism exists to allow a positive macro surprise to flip the call up. The result is a flat call that misses both the absolute move (+1.19% XLRE) and the relative outcome (+0.14% rel) when the ISM beat rips the broad market.
CORRECTED_BEHAVIOR: When a same-day two-sided macro catalyst is identified, treat it as a magnitude-expansion risk, not a magnitude cap. If the catalyst is high-impact (ISM Services, CPI, NFP) and the sector has been a relative laggard with no fresh negative catalyst, the flat band should be widened to at least mild on both sides, and the confidence should be reduced rather than the magnitude capped. Additionally, when the broad market rips on a macro beat, relative laggards with duration sensitivity (XLRE) can still post positive absolute moves — the flat call must not be anchored to the relative tape when the absolute driver is a macro surprise that was explicitly identified but not pre-scored. The tape sleeve should be allowed to confirm an up-side macro surprise when S0-S3 are zero and the catalyst is high-impact, rather than being restricted to down-side confirmation only.
EVIDENCE: Actual XLRE +1.19% vs SPY +1.05% (rel +0.14%). The model predicted flat/flat with total_score −0.45. The ISM Services beat (consensus ~54.2–54.3 vs prior 54.1) was explicitly identified as two-sided and unprinted, then used as a confidence/mag cap. The broad-market rip on the beat carried XLRE to +1.19% absolute — a magnitude miss of the entire flat band. The relative outcome (+0.14%) was actually positive, meaning the sector did not underperform on the day despite the 1d/1w/1m relative laggard tape. The model's refusal to pre-score the catalyst was correct in direction (it did not know the beat), but the flat band was too narrow for a high-impact catalyst day.
LESSON_MATCH_CHECK: Matches sibling lessons from 2026-09-03 across sectors (basic_materials, communication_services, consumer_cyclical, consumer_defensive, energy, financial, healthcare, industrials) — all show the same pattern: two-sided macro catalyst identified, refused pre-scoring, flat/flat predicted, broad-market rip on the beat produces large absolute moves that miss the flat band. This is a systematic error across sectors on the same day, confirming the trigger pattern is generalizable and not sector-specific.
BACKWARD_CHECK: Would this lesson have helped on 2026-08-28 (down/mild, actual −0.40%, dir HIT)? On that day, no high-impact two-sided macro catalyst was identified as a same-day event — the model correctly predicted down/mild on rates-up tape. The lesson would not have changed that call. Would it have helped on 2026-08-26 (up/flat, actual −0.60%, dir MISS)? That was a rates-up day where the model incorrectly predicted up — the lesson is about macro-surprise days, not rates-driven days, so it would not have prevented that miss. The lesson is specific to high-impact two-sided catalyst days and does not conflict with prior correct calls.
CONFLICT_CHECK: The lesson conflicts with the standing rule "do not pre-score two-sided unprinted catalysts" — but it does not overturn that rule. The model should still not pre-score the direction of the catalyst. The lesson only changes the magnitude band and confidence treatment: when a high-impact two-sided catalyst is identified, the flat band is too narrow regardless of direction. This is consistent with the existing "confidence/mag cap" encoding — the cap should be a widening, not a narrowing, when the catalyst is high-impact. No conflict with 08-21 (level-vs-change), 08-25 (do not force down), or 08-27 (no up license) — those lessons govern rates-driven days, not macro-surprise days.
FALSIFIER: A future session where a high-impact two-sided macro catalyst is identified (ISM Services, CPI, NFP), the model widens the band to mild on both sides, and the actual session delivers a flat outcome (|move| < 0.5%) — that would falsify the lesson's claim that high-impact catalysts require wider bands. Also falsifiable if a session with a high-impact catalyst and a flat band prediction produces a correct flat call while a widened-band alternative would have been wrong.
DIVERGENCE_VERDICT: none_flagged — the model did not flag divergence (leading_sum = 0, divergence_flagged = False), but the actual outcome showed the leading factors were wrong in magnitude, not direction. The tape sleeve (S4 = −1) was the only non-zero factor and was treated as confirmation-only, barred from flipping factors — but the actual session showed the tape was wrong (XLRE +1.19% absolute) and the macro catalyst was the true driver. This is a case where the model's divergence framework (leading vs tape) failed to anticipate that a high-impact macro catalyst could override both.
ACTIVE_LESSON_REVIEW: 08-21 (level-vs-change, cap S0/S1 at 0) — correctly applied, rates were not the driver. 08-25 (do not force down off FRED table) — correctly applied, the model did not force down. 08-27 (no up license from ES/NQ green) — this lesson may have contributed to the miss by forbidding an up call on flat futures, but the actual driver was the ISM beat, not the futures tape. 08-18 (relative bid is a mag cap) — the model applied this to cap magnitude at flat, but the actual session had no relative bid at the open and still delivered +1.19% absolute on the macro rip. The lesson's "no relative bid = no up" logic failed when the absolute driver was a macro surprise. 08-28 (do not import XLF/XLY leftover bans) — correctly applied. The active lessons were mostly correct for rates-driven days but did not cover the macro-surprise scenario.
